intent: Fix a race where two concurrent addrConn.connect() calls both saw Idle and started parallel transport attempts, by having callers hold ac.mu across the Idle check and resetTransportAndUnlock (which now owns and releases the lock). Fixes #7365.
residual_risks: updateAddrs now returns while the spawned goroutine owns ac.mu; the deferred ac.transport.GracefulClose() (holds the old transport's mutex, onClose waits on ac.mu) blocks until the goroutine reaches its Unlock after setting Connecting. No deadlock found: that goroutine path never takes the old transport's mutex or waits on the caller. Cost is added scheduling latency in the old transport's close path. (adversarial)
Lock ownership transfer is enforced only by the doc comment and a runtime panic on double/missing unlock; no static or test guard (discussed and accepted in PR thread).
testing_gaps: No test added: the race is only exercised by the flaky Test/AuthorityRevive (~0.4% failure rate before the fix); no deterministic regression test for concurrent addrConn.connect() calls producing a single transport.
